transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello. Well, I'm here today because... I just can't seem to turn off my worrying once it starts. It's really frustrating. I'll tell myself that I've already made the list, I've checked the dates, and I've done everything I reasonably can, but my mind just won't stop dwelling on things.
Do you find that your worrying tends to happen more in social situations, or does it occur even when you're alone and not interacting with others?

Oh, it happens even when I'm completely alone. It's not really tied to being around other people at all. I could just be sitting by myself at home, and... well, my mind just keeps roaming. 

It'll jump from an exhibition schedule I'm looking at, to my daughter's travel plans, to suddenly worrying about whether the house gutters need fixing. It's like these small things just start to feel as if they could unravel into something much bigger, even when there's no one else around to trigger it.
Do you notice any physical symptoms, like restlessness, muscle tension, or trouble sleeping, when you're worrying like this?

Yes, I do notice that. I get quite restless, actually. I often feel... well, just wound up, even when I'm just in my own living room. 

If I'm on a phone call, I'll catch myself tapping my fingers the whole time. Or I'll just keep getting up to straighten something on a table, mostly because sitting quietly makes me feel jumpy. It's just hard to stay still when my mind is going like that.
Do these worries tend to focus on a variety of everyday things, or do they often center around one specific concern or theme?

It's definitely a variety of everyday things. There isn't really one specific concern that I focus on. Like I mentioned earlier, it just... bounces around. One minute it's the house, the next it's a schedule, or just checking in on my family. It's really just whatever ordinary thing happens to cross my mind that day, rather than one big theme.
How long have you been experiencing this kind of constant worrying and restlessness?

It's been about seven months now. It really started shortly after a friend of mine passed away. We had some projects we were working on together, and I was trying to just... keep things moving forward by myself. That's when I noticed this constant worrying and feeling so wound up all the time began.
Do you find it difficult to control or stop the worrying once it starts, even when you know the thoughts might not make sense?

Yes, I really do. Honestly, that's a big part of what brings me in to see you. I just... I can’t seem to turn off the worrying once it starts. I'll sit there and tell myself that I’ve already made the list, I've checked the dates, and I've done all I reasonably can do to handle whatever it is. But even knowing all that, I just can't make my mind stop dwelling on it.
Have these worries and feelings of restlessness made it harder for you to function normally, like doing your work, enjoying time with family, or taking care of daily tasks at home?

Well, yes, a little bit. I mean, I still keep up with the garden and my book club. But lately, I've started arriving to the club less prepared than I normally would be. And... I've actually been turning down parts of the exhibition planning that I usually help with. It just feels a lot harder to manage all those details than it used to.
Have there been times when you felt unusually upbeat, overly energetic, or irritable, where you were doing things more quickly or energetically than usual?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. I mean, I wouldn't say I've felt unusually upbeat or had bursts of energy. If anything, I've just felt more... worn out from all the worrying. I certainly haven't been doing things faster than normal.
Do you find that your worries are often about a number of different events or activities, such as work, family, chores, or other responsibilities, rather than just one specific thing?

Yes, it's definitely a mix of things. It's never just one specific issue. My mind just keeps... roaming, I suppose. I'll be worrying about the exhibition schedule, and then I'm thinking about my daughter's travel plans, or even just wondering if the house gutters need fixing. It seems like these small things just start to feel as if they could unravel into something much bigger.
Have you noticed any trouble focusing or keeping your attention on tasks because of your worrying?

Not really, no. I mean, I haven't noticed any trouble with my focus. I can still sit down and read for my book club or pay attention to what I'm doing out in the garden. The worries are definitely there in the background, but they don't really stop me from keeping my mind on the task right in front of me.
Would you say that you feel excessive anxiety or worry on more days than not for at least several weeks at a time?

Yes, I would say so. It's definitely more days than not. This has actually been going on for about seven months now. It started... well, shortly after my friend passed away, and I was trying to keep our projects moving along. Since then, the worry has just been pretty constant.
Have you noticed any symptoms like sweating, a racing heart, or shortness of breath when you're feeling anxious or worried?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. Um, my heart doesn't race, and I don't get out of breath or start sweating. It's mostly just... well, just the worrying itself. I don't really get those kinds of physical reactions.
Have you had trouble falling asleep or staying asleep because your mind is too busy worrying?

No, my sleep has been fine, actually. I haven't had any trouble falling asleep or waking up in the middle of the night. Even with the worrying, once my head hits the pillow, I usually sleep right through.
Do you find it difficult to relax, even when you have time to yourself and no pressing responsibilities?

Yes, I do. Well, I often feel pretty wound up, even just sitting in my own living room. I'll notice I'm tapping my fingers during phone calls, or I'll just get up to straighten something out around the house. It seems like sitting quietly just makes me feel a bit jumpy, even when there's absolutely nothing I need to be doing.
Do you feel like you have very little control over your worrying, even when you try hard to stop it?

Yes, that's exactly it. Honestly, that's really what brings me in. I just can’t seem to turn off the worrying once it starts. I'll sit there and tell myself that I’ve made the list, I've checked the dates, and I’ve done all I reasonably can do about a situation... but it doesn't matter. Even when I try to talk myself down, I just don't have much control over it.
Even though you mentioned your sleep has been fine overall, have you ever found it hard to fall asleep or stay asleep because your mind is too busy worrying?

No, like I mentioned a little bit ago, I really don't have any trouble with that. I know it probably seems a bit odd since my mind is so busy during the day, but honestly, my sleep is completely fine. I just don't lie awake at night worrying.
